title: Closed-support restriction as the exceptional counit mate
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes, let $h:X'\to X$ be any scheme morphism, and form the Cartesian square with $Z'=X'\times_XZ$, $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $g:Z'\to Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. No finite-type hypothesis on $h$ or $X'$ is imposed. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves and their bounded-below ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $F\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $a\in\mathbf Z$, and set $K=Ri^!F[a]$ and $K'=Ri'^!h^*F[a]$, with the closed ambient right adjoints [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Write $\varepsilon:i_*K\to F[a]$ and $\varepsilon_{i'}:i'_*K'\to h^*F[a]$ for the counits, and use the canonical shift comparisons.

The finite closed direct-image exchange gives a natural $A$-linear isomorphism $b_B:h^*i_*B\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_*g^*B$ on these complexes. Define $\varepsilon'=h^*\varepsilon\circ b_K^{-1}$ and let $\beta:g^*K\to K'$ be its exceptional adjunct. For $\alpha\in H^a_Z(X,F)$ [def-pur-support-cohomology], put $M=\chi_{i,F}^a(\alpha):i_*A_Z\to F[a]$, using the canonical etale supported-Hom identification [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback, lem-amb-closed-support-hom], and let $u:A_Z\to K$ be its exceptional adjunct. With $c=b_{A_Z}:h^*i_*A_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_*A_{Z'}$, put $M'=h^*M\circ c^{-1}$. Then
$$M=\varepsilon\circ i_*u,\qquad M'=\varepsilon'\circ i'_*g^*u,\qquad \varepsilon_{i'}\circ i'_*\beta=\varepsilon',\qquad \operatorname{adj}_{i'}(M')=\beta\circ g^*u.$$
Moreover $M'=\chi_{i',h^*F}^a(h^*\alpha)$ with the supported pullback of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback]. Thus restriction of the adjunct, defined using the counit mate, represents the pulled-back supported class without assuming $\beta$ invertible.

For $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], apply the canonical supported-constant, pullback and shift comparisons of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] to the inverse images of these etale objects. The same four equations and supported-class identification hold there; the induced restriction of $\nu_Z^*u$ is the image of $\beta\circ g^*u$. When $i$ is a closed immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes, this is the restriction for the transported functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. At an arbitrary geometric fibre the exceptional object means $\nu_{Z'}^*Ri'^!h^*F[a]$, using the ordinary closed adjoint without a finite-type assumption on the fibre. This assertion is only about etale-origin objects and does not posit an ambient pro-etale adjunction.

proof.text: The base change $i'$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and both $i$ and $i'$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Apply [sk-lem-pbc-finite] with coefficient ring $A$: direct image is exact and its canonical derived exchange is the natural isomorphism $b_B:h^*i_*B\to i'_*g^*B$. Constant-coefficient inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Thus these functors act termwise on derived objects, with the shift comparisons of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The right adjoints supplied by [lem-exc-closed-ambient] preserve lower bounds by part (1) of [lem-pur-exact-derived-adjunction-bounds], applied to the exact functors $i_*,i'_*$. Hence all objects used below lie in $D^+$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique] to identify $Ri^!(F[a])$ with $(Ri^!F)[a]$, and likewise for $i'$, with their counits. No property of $h$ other than being a scheme morphism has entered.

proof.text: For an adjunction $L\dashv R$ with counit $e$, the inverse Hom bijection sends $v:P\to RN$ to $e_N\circ L(v)$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Apply it to the definition of $u=\operatorname{adj}_i(M)$ to obtain $M=\varepsilon\circ i_*u$. Apply it to the definition of $\beta=\operatorname{adj}_{i'}(\varepsilon')$ to obtain $\varepsilon_{i'}\circ i'_*\beta=\varepsilon'$. These are the first and third equations, with the shifted counits fixed in step 1.

proof.text:
Naturality of $b$ at $u:A_Z\to K$ gives $b_K\circ h^*(i_*u)=i'_*g^*u\circ c$, since $c=b_{A_Z}$ under $g^*A_Z=A_{Z'}$. Multiply by the inverse isomorphisms on the appropriate sides to get $h^*(i_*u)\circ c^{-1}=b_K^{-1}\circ i'_*g^*u$. Substituting the first equation into the definition of $M'$ now gives
$$M'=h^*(\varepsilon)\circ h^*(i_*u)\circ c^{-1}=h^*(\varepsilon)\circ b_K^{-1}\circ i'_*g^*u=\varepsilon'\circ i'_*g^*u.$$
This is precisely naturality of the canonical finite exchange of [sk-lem-pbc-finite], followed by associativity and inverse cancellation.

source.place: Tag 0959, canonical finite exchange; agent-written naturality calculation at u.

proof.text:
Functoriality of $i'_*$ and the equations already proved give
$$\varepsilon_{i'}\circ i'_*(\beta\circ g^*u)=(\varepsilon_{i'}\circ i'_*\beta)\circ i'_*g^*u=\varepsilon'\circ i'_*g^*u=M'.$$
The inverse adjunction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] is a bijection. Applying its inverse to this equality proves $\operatorname{adj}_{i'}(M')=\beta\circ g^*u$. Only $b$ was inverted; no inverse to $\beta$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0037, bijectivity and inverse counit formula; agent-written substitution.

proof.text:
Apply the etale assertion of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] to $h,i,F,a,\alpha$. Its hypotheses permit arbitrary $X'$ and $h$, and its canonical exchange $c$ is exactly $b_{A_Z}$ by the definition of finite exchange in step 1. Its displayed equation is
$$\chi_{i',h^*F}^a(h^*\alpha)=h^*(\chi_{i,F}^a(\alpha))\circ c^{-1}=M'.$$
Consequently the adjunct in step 4 represents the pulled-back supported class. The supported-Hom identification here is the ordinary etale one induced by the closed-support cone, as explicitly specified in the cited statement, rather than an identification between different sites.

source.place: Theorem 9.4 and its Ext proof, Example 9.5, pp. 65-67; explicit derived pullback compatibility is the cited refinement.

proof.text: Put $C_T=\nu_T^*$. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], $C_T$ induces a functor on $D^+$, respects composition and shifts, and preserves each of the four equations. To read their endpoints, let $t_{i,B}:C_X i_*B\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_{\mathrm{proet},*}C_ZB$ be [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], and similarly for $i'$. The hypotheses hold: a finite morphism is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and affine morphisms are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. No quasi-compactness of the complementary open is needed. Let $k_g:C_{Z'}g^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_Z$ and $k_h:C_{X'}h^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_X$ be [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. All equations on the pro-etale side mean these images, conjugated by $t$, $k$ and the supported-constant comparisons. Naturality of the endpoint isomorphisms ensures that internal comparisons cancel between successive factors.

source.place: Tag 099R, section-comparison, via the cited bounded-below direct-image and inverse-image comparisons; coefficient exactness uses Tag 04JC.

proof.text:
More explicitly the compared restriction of $C_Zu$ is
$$C_{Z'}A_{Z'}\xrightarrow{C_{Z'}(g^*u)}C_{Z'}g^*K\xrightarrow{C_{Z'}\beta}C_{Z'}K'.$$
Equivalently its factors are $g_{\mathrm{proet}}^*(C_Zu)$ followed by $C_{Z'}\beta\circ k_{g,K}^{-1}$, with source comparison $k_{g,A_Z}$; naturality of $k_g$ gives the displayed composite. It is therefore the image of $\beta\circ g^*u$. The pro-etale and site-comparison clauses of [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback] identify $C_XM$ and $C_{X'}M'$ (precomposed with the supported-constant comparisons) with the corresponding supported classes, and state that these comparisons commute with $h^*$ and $c$. Thus the image of $M'$ is exactly the pro-etale pulled-back supported class. This establishes the asserted class identification as well as the four image equations, without invoking any pro-etale exceptional adjunction.

source.place: Theorem 9.4 and Example 9.5; agent-written site transport using the full supported-Hom pullback statement.

proof.text: Finally suppose $i$ is between finite-type $k$-schemes. For the closed compactification $(1_Z,i)$, ordinary etale compact support is $Ri_*=i_*$, so its right adjoint is the closed $Ri^!$ of [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. The finite formula in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is $C_ZRi^!R\nu_{X,*}$. The site-comparison unit $F\xrightarrow{\sim}R\nu_{X,*}C_XF$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies its value on $C_XF$ with $C_ZRi^!F$. Its Hom transpose on an etale-origin source is the ordinary etale transpose followed by $C_Z$: full faithfulness of $C_X,C_Z$ and the direct-image comparison of step 6 identify the two Hom sets. Hence the restriction of step 7 is exactly the restriction of this transported functor. For an arbitrary geometric fibre retain $C_{Z'}Ri'^!h^*F[a]$ and the map $C_{Z'}\beta$ constructed above; steps 1-7 already apply to this fibre, even when it has no finite-type $k$-scheme structure. This proves the final domain qualification without extending the transported functor's definition. The origin theorem is proved by the general counit identity: after transporting the first adjunction along compactNormalization.symm, uniqueness of right adjoints sends adj(M) followed by R(eta) to the transpose of compactNormalization.hom followed by M followed by eta. Apply comparison(P,Z), preservation of composition, and the definition of originIso with eta the actual comparison unit. The first seven steps remain pending in the main theorem.
